title: Festival History and Frequently Asked Questions
text: Public Ganeshotsav in Pune was started in 1893 by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak as a way to unite people against British colonial rule under the guise of religious celebration, since public gatherings were otherwise restricted. The festival lasts 10 days, ending with Anant Chaturdashi visarjan (immersion) processions that can run for over 24 continuous hours through the central Pune route via Laxmi Road, Tulshibaug and the Mula-Mutha riverbank ghats. Frequently asked questions: Q: Can foreigners/tourists attend darshan? A: Yes, all mandals are open to the public regardless of religion or nationality, though modest dress is appreciated. Q: Is photography allowed? A: Generally yes near the mandap, but flash photography and drones are restricted near some large mandals like Dagdusheth Halwai for crowd safety. Q: Are mobile phones allowed inside barricaded queues? A: Yes, but jewelry and valuables should be secured due to dense crowding.
